chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The صاحب of this matter — none names him by his name except a disbeliever.

key_terms.الْأَمْرِ: the matter or command; here, the divinely ordained authority
key_terms.صَاحِبُ: the possessor or master; here, the one vested with this divine matter
key_terms.كَافِرٌ: a disbeliever; one characterized here by rejection
key_terms.هَذَا: this; indicating a specific, known religious matter

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in al-Kafi say about naming the صاحب of this أمر by his name?
ai.summary: This hadith states a prohibition concerning explicitly naming the صاحب of this أمر by his personal name. In Shia theological context, it reflects the sanctity and guarded status of the Imam and signals the seriousness attached to preserving the divinely designated authority.
